title: Dark energy and the expansion of the universe
summary: Distances to galaxies and supernovae measure how fast the universe expanded at each epoch, and so what dark energy does.

concepts.label: Cosmological model
concepts.description: A flat universe of matter (Ωm), radiation and dark energy with equation of state w(z) = w0 + wa·z/(1+z); ΛCDM is w0 = −1, wa = 0.

children.label: Dark energy
children.description: Whatever accelerates the expansion: a cosmological constant (w = −1) or something that evolves.

children.label: Hubble constant
children.description: Today's expansion rate H0, km/s per megaparsec.

concepts.label: Baryon acoustic oscillations
concepts.description: Sound waves in the early plasma left a preferred separation, the sound horizon r_d ≈ 147 Mpc, between galaxies: a standard ruler.

children.label: Comoving distance DM and Hubble distance DH
children.description: DM: distance across the line of sight; DH = c/H(z): along it; DV: their average. Divided by r_d.

concepts.label: Type Ia supernova
concepts.description: An exploding white dwarf of nearly standard peak brightness: a standard candle. Pantheon+ compiles 1,701 light curves.

concepts.label: Cosmic microwave background
concepts.description: Light from z ≈ 1090; its acoustic angle θ* is the sound horizon seen at that distance.
